nodes.name: Kart rigid body
nodes.purpose: Per-update rigid body step for every kart: force and torque accumulation, trapezoid angular integration, drag, top speed clamp and pose composition

nodes.name: Wheel suspension
nodes.purpose: Four spring-damper wheel struts that hold the body above the ground, measure travel against the collision result and ease the tyre radius down on sink surfaces

nodes.name: Kart surface response
nodes.purpose: Reads field collision attributes into kart surface state and applies the resulting wrench: floor type, boost pads, jump pads, halfpipe ramps, walls and body hitboxes

nodes.name: Course mesh collision
nodes.purpose: Packed attribute prisms, the block tree that indexes them, point and sphere narrow phase, and the cached repeat queries every kart part goes through

nodes.name: Object and drivable collision
nodes.purpose: Collision against course objects and movable drivable props, each with its own local mesh, placement matrix and spatial cache

nodes.name: CPU driver
nodes.purpose: CPU path following around a bump: alignment of the impact with the body forward axis, a scaled backward path offset, and trick requests while airborne

nodes.name: Lap and ghost progress
nodes.purpose: Sector crossing over course checkpoints and the recorded input stream that replays a time trial ghost

cards.name: Force to velocity integration
cards.summary: One step turns the force total on a kart into external velocity, then into a world-space displacement, with a fixed drag ratio and a hit state that clears vertical motion
cards.behavior: Every force registered on the body is summed into one total before the step begins. Acceleration is that total, and the external velocity gains acceleration scaled by the delta time the physics engine supplies, so the same routine runs at whatever step the race loop chooses. While the body carries a recent-hit flag the vertical part of the external velocity is cleared, which keeps a strike from launching a kart upward, and a second flag applies the same clamp for scripted recovery states. The external velocity is then multiplied by a drag ratio once per update before it is combined with internal velocity and with the road and water carry velocities. The combined vector is both the per-update displacement written to the position and the source of the signed speed the rest of the code reads. A horizontal projection of the external velocity onto the body's facing also produces a speed fix whose sign tells forward travel from reverse.

constants.name: external velocity drag
constants.unit: ratio per update; the step rate is supplied by the race loop and is unverified

constants.name: vertical velocity cleared while hit
constants.unit: units per update, applied on each update after a hit

constants.name: default vertical force term
constants.unit: force units per update, added to the body total before integration

cards.name: Top speed clamp and airborne cap
cards.summary: The integrated speed is capped at the allowance the controller passes in, the allowance shrinks with a squashed model, and airborne vertical motion is clipped
cards.behavior: After the displacement vector is assembled the step measures its length and caps it at the top speed the kart controller handed in, so a boost and gravity together can never exceed the current allowance. When the model scale along the body third axis is below one, the allowance itself is multiplied by that scale, which slows a squashed kart without touching its authored top speed. Vertical internal velocity gathered while airborne is clipped before it is folded into the displacement, so a large step cannot turn the kart\'s own stored motion into an unintended launch. The normalised speed vector stays with the body for the rest of the update because wheel contact and collision response both read it to separate forward sliding from sideways sliding.

constants.name: airborne vertical internal velocity cap
constants.unit: units per update, clamped every update while the kart is airborne

constants.name: scale threshold for allowance scaling
constants.unit: model scale ratio, tested every update

cards.name: Angular motion and upright limits
cards.summary: Torque is integrated into angular velocity with a trapezoid step, damped, clamped per axis, then folded into the body orientation quaternion with an upright pass on top
cards.behavior: Torque arrives in the body frame, is turned into angular acceleration by the cached inverse inertia tensor, and is integrated with a trapezoid rule that evaluates the angular velocity twice per update so a single strong impulse cannot overshoot. The result is damped by a fixed ratio, clamped independently on each of the three axes, and multiplied by the body angular factor before it is composed with the transient and special rotations into the orientation quaternion. Composition happens in the body frame, the quaternion is renormalised, and the same orientation supplies the body axes the camera and wheel code read. Bodies flagged to stay upright run a stabilising pass toward an interpolated up vector after integration, which pulls a tilted kart back onto its wheels instead of letting the step tumble it, while the bike body zeroes its third-axis angular velocity outright.

constants.name: angular velocity damping
constants.unit: ratio per update; the step rate is supplied by the caller and is unverified

constants.name: first axis angular clamp
constants.unit: radians per second, clamped every update

constants.name: second axis angular clamp
constants.unit: radians per second, clamped every update

constants.name: third axis angular clamp
constants.unit: radians per second, clamped every update

constants.name: trapezoid weighting
constants.unit: dimensionless weight, applied once per update

constants.name: upright stabilisation factor
constants.unit: ratio per update, applied while the body is flagged upright

cards.name: Box inertia tensor
cards.summary: A kart resists turning according to the box it occupies: two extents give a diagonal inertia tensor whose inverse is cached for the torque solve
cards.behavior: Body setup takes two vectors describing the kart box and builds a diagonal inertia tensor from them. Each diagonal term starts with a twelfth of the sum of the squares of the other two components of the first vector, and the second vector contributes its own squared components, so the two inputs play the roles of the box dimensions and an offset mass. The tensor is kept diagonal and its inverse is computed once at setup, which turns every later torque solve into a matrix-vector product with no division. Because only the diagonal terms exist, resistance to pitch, yaw and roll are three independent numbers, and a body that is long in one direction resists turning about the matching axis more than a compact one. The inverse is what the angular integration and the angular-acceleration helper handed to collision response both read, so the same numbers decide how far a hit spins a kart rather than shoves it.

constants.name: box inertia divisor
constants.unit: dimensionless divisor, applied once when the body is set up

constants.name: default angular velocity factor
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier per update

cards.name: Spring-damper suspension strut
cards.summary: Each wheel hangs on a spring and damper measured against the strut travel, and the resulting force is applied as a wrench at the strut top with the floor plane accounted for
cards.behavior: The strut measures travel along its down direction between the wheel centre and the suspension top. While the wheel collision info reports a floor, the strut builds a force from the wheel spring stiffness times the travel still available plus the damper times the closing speed, then projects the horizontal part of that force back onto the floor plane so a banked or tilted surface still pushes the kart up rather than sideways. The vertical part is capped by the kart maximum vertical acceleration, dropped entirely when the body vertical external velocity is above a threshold, and dropped again while a flag disables vertical suspension so scripted moments and trick rotation stay readable. The force is applied at the suspension top as a wrench, with the pitch torque optionally suppressed for flips and wheelies, which is what makes a landing on one wheel twist the chassis instead of lifting it evenly. During a respawn the vertical component is clamped to a small symmetric limit so the kart cannot be fired through the floor while it is being placed back on the course.

constants.name: vertical external velocity that disables suspension force
constants.unit: units per second at the caller integration step; step rate unverified

constants.name: respawn vertical force clamp
constants.unit: force units, applied every update while the respawn timer runs

constants.name: travel speed shaping blend
constants.unit: ratio per update

constants.name: floor approach speed that enables travel shaping
constants.unit: units per update, tested every update while a floor is held

cards.name: Wheel travel limits and tyre squash
cards.summary: Wheel travel is clamped between zero and the scaled strut maximum, the wheel velocity has every carried motion removed, and the tyre radius eases down under sink depth
cards.behavior: Travel is measured along the strut down direction between the wheel centre and the suspension top, clamped to the strut maximum after the vehicle vertical scale is applied, and floored at zero so a wheel can never pull the body downward. The wheel position is rebuilt from that travel, and its velocity is taken as the difference from the previous position minus the body internal velocity, the moving road and water carry velocities, the body collision movement and the kart collision displacement, leaving only motion caused by the ground under the wheel. When the narrow phase reports a floor, the wheel is pushed out along the contact tangent and the target tyre radius shrinks by the surface sink depth multiplied by a global sink factor, so soft ground visibly swallows part of the wheel. The current radius approaches that target with a fixed easing ratio rather than snapping, which keeps a landing from producing a one-update pop in the tyre.

constants.name: tyre radius easing
constants.unit: ratio per update

constants.name: travel margin above the previous travel
constants.unit: world units, applied per update before the collision clamp

constants.name: minimum wheel travel
constants.unit: world units, clamped every update

cards.name: Wheel probe sphere and scrub
cards.summary: Each wheel collides through one small sphere pushed ahead of its centre, and the contact result drives a floor moment whose lateral rate collapses during a wall scrape
cards.behavior: A wheel is not a mesh in the collision pass: it is a single sphere of fixed radius, centred slightly forward of the wheel position so the probe leads the wheel along the body facing. The forward offset scales with the wheel radius, the body lean and the kart total scale, so a light and a heavy kart probe alike only when their lean matches. Probe velocity is the collision force scaled by the delta time and a per-update factor, which lets the probe track the floor without being dragged along by the kart own speed. Once a floor is held, a floor moment is applied with a lateral rate taken from the collision state, and that rate falls to a much smaller value while the kart is scraping a wall, giving the characteristic loss of grip in a wall grind. Applying the moment can suppress the angular velocity change during a flip or a wheelie, so authored special states keep their rotation.

constants.name: wheel probe sphere radius
constants.unit: world units, fixed per wheel at setup

constants.name: probe forward offset factor
constants.unit: ratio of the wheel radius, applied every update

constants.name: probe contact velocity factor
constants.unit: per second at the caller delta time; step rate unverified

constants.name: wall-scrape lateral rate
constants.unit: ratio per update

constants.name: wheel hitbox height above the body origin
constants.unit: world units, fixed per wheel

cards.name: Floor attribute classification
cards.summary: One packed attribute word per floor prism decides speed factor, handling factor, sink depth, trick availability and the surface markers a kart carries for the update
cards.behavior: The collision mesh stores one attribute word per prism. The low five bits name the surface type, the next three bits name a variant of that type, and two further bits carry a sink-depth step. The kart reads the type as an index into its own per-surface tables, keeps the smallest speed factor seen when several wheels touch different surfaces, accumulates handling factors, and copies the sink depth so the tyre can shrink later. Three high bits classify special behaviour: a trickable flag that permits an air trick off the surface, a road-reject flag that is passed on to the kart state, and a soft-wall flag that marks a forgiving boundary. Offroad surfaces set an offroad marker, moving road sets its own marker, sticky road sets a state flag, and the winning prism type mask is kept so later code can ask what kind of ground was just found.

constants.name: attribute type field mask
constants.unit: bit mask, applied once per collision query

constants.name: attribute variant mask
constants.unit: bit mask, applied after a five-bit shift once per query

constants.name: sink depth field shift
constants.unit: bit position, applied once per query

constants.name: trickable attribute bit
constants.unit: bit mask, tested once per floor contact

constants.name: road reject attribute bit
constants.unit: bit mask, tested once per floor contact

constants.name: soft wall attribute bit
constants.unit: bit mask, tested once per floor and wall contact

cards.name: Boost pads and boost ramps
cards.summary: A floor type of boost pad or boost ramp sets the matching pad bit on the kart, captures the ramp variant and marks the contact as trickable
cards.behavior: Two floor types push a kart forward without an item: the flat boost pad and the boost ramp. The pad is detected on wheel contacts only, so the body alone passing over it does nothing, and it sets the boost panel bit in the kart pad mask. A boost ramp sets a different bit, records its variant number for the pad handler to interpret, and additionally raises the trickable surface marker so a trick can be pulled on the way off it. Both surfaces raise the boost panel surface marker, the ramp also raises its own marker, and on any floor without a ramp bit the stored ramp type is reset to an invalid value. Because pad detection rides on the same attribute read as the surface tables, a pad laid on soft ground applies its boost and the ground sink depth in the same update.

constants.name: boost panel pad bit
constants.unit: bit mask, set once per wheel contact on a pad

constants.name: boost ramp pad bit
constants.unit: bit mask, set once per wheel contact on a ramp

constants.name: boost panel surface marker
constants.unit: bit mask, set once per contact update

constants.name: neutral speed factor
constants.unit: ratio, the value held before surface tables are read each update

cards.name: Jump pads and trampolines
cards.summary: A jump-pad floor type arms a pad bit and stores the pad variant unless the kart is already riding a pad, and marks the contact trickable
cards.behavior: A jump pad is read from the same attribute word as any other floor. The pad is armed only when the kart is not simultaneously resting on the ground and already on a pad, and only when the velocity-increase variant is not already active, so a kart sitting on the pad cannot retrigger it every update. Arming writes the jump pad bit into the pad mask and stores the attribute variant as the pad type, which the movement layer later turns into a launch impulse. The contact is also flagged trickable, which is how a trick can start from a trampoline even though the surface itself is not a ramp. A kart that reaches the pad already carrying the velocity-increase state passes through without a second launch, because that flag alone blocks arming.

constants.name: jump pad floor type index
constants.unit: attribute type index, read once per floor contact

constants.name: jump pad pad bit
constants.unit: bit mask, set once per arming contact

constants.name: jump pad query bit shift
constants.unit: bit shift, applied once per query

cards.name: Halfpipe ramps
cards.summary: Halfpipe ramp surfaces switch a kart into the halfpipe state, start a short invisibility window and hand a local kart a boost panel on the variant that carries one
cards.behavior: A halfpipe ramp is its own floor type. Touching it sets the halfpipe ramp flag, and also the local variant of that flag unless the kart is an online remote copy, which stops a networked opponent from claiming local halfpipe effects. The surface marker is raised for the effects layer and the kart halfpipe invisibility timer is set to a couple of frames, a short window the collision layer holds on the kart. Variant one of the type also sets the boost panel bit, which is how some halfpipes give speed on entry rather than only on exit. The same attribute read runs the trickable test afterwards, so a ramp and the geometry around it can independently allow air tricks while the halfpipe state is active.

constants.name: halfpipe invisibility timer
constants.unit: frames at the game update rate, set once per ramp contact

constants.name: halfpipe ramp floor type
constants.unit: attribute type index, read once per floor contact

constants.name: halfpipe ramp surface marker
constants.unit: bit mask, set once per contact update

cards.name: Wall contact and bump cooldown
cards.summary: Wall types pass two category masks, soft walls soften the contact bookkeeping, and two karts cannot exchange bump impulses on consecutive updates
cards.behavior: Wall classification asks two masks in order. The first decides whether a wall participates in player collision at all; the second decides whether the prism records its type and variant and whether it is soft. Soft walls accumulate the suspension bottom height over the frames of the contact and keep the hard-wall frame counter from advancing, which is how a forgiving boundary avoids being counted as a hard hit. A separate timer forbids the same pair of karts from exchanging bump impulses more often than once every ten frames, and an out-of-bounds counter is documented as allowing three frames of solid out-of-bounds contact before the respawn path takes over. The kart collision bounding radius is refreshed from the largest hitbox extent times the current hitbox scale, so a shrunken kart presents a smaller wall target in the same update.

constants.name: player bump cooldown
constants.unit: frames at the game update rate, between two bumps of the same pair

constants.name: solid out-of-bounds contact window
constants.unit: frames at the game update rate

constants.name: default collision bounding radius
constants.unit: world units, replaced on the first bounding update by the hitbox extent

constants.name: default lateral floor rate
constants.unit: ratio per update

cards.name: Body hitbox rig
cards.summary: A body collides as a fixed set of spheres whose world positions follow body scale, total scale and sink depth, and whose extents produce one bounding radius
cards.behavior: A kart body collision shape is a fixed set of up to sixteen spheres declared beside the model, each with a local position, a radius, a wall-only flag and an optional tyre index. Every update the spheres are re-placed: the local position is scaled by the body scale, lifted by the current sink depth, lifted again by the extra elevation that appears when the body is scaled down relative to the kart total scale, then rotated with the body and offset by its position. Scaling the group multiplies every sphere radius, which is what lets a mushroom-sized kart strike walls a normal kart would clear. The bounding radius is the largest single sphere extent plus its offset, computed once when the group is built, and the same limit calculation also returns half of the deepest extent. Because placement is rebuilt from the current pose every update, a spinning kart sweeps its spheres through the same geometry its model shows.

constants.name: spheres in a body rig
constants.unit: spheres, fixed by the model data

constants.name: hitbox group default scale
constants.unit: ratio, set once at setup

constants.name: collision depth fraction
constants.unit: ratio of the deepest sphere extent, computed once per rig

cards.name: Attribute block lookup
cards.summary: A packed course mesh finds candidate prisms by indexing the query position into a block tree whose inner nodes carry child offsets and whose leaves carry prism lists
cards.behavior: Course collision data is stored as position, normal and prism arrays plus a block tree. A query subtracts the mesh minimum corner from the point and checks three axis masks that describe the tree extent; a non-zero result means the point lies outside the tree and the lookup returns nothing. Inside, the point coordinates are shifted by the mesh shift widths and packed from the three axes into an index, and the traversal walks the tree: a node whose stored offset has its top bit set is a leaf, while any other value gives the byte offset to the next node and, after the shift is decremented, the child index. The leaf low thirty-one bits address the prism index list for that cell. The bounding box used by these checks is built by expanding over the three vertices of every prism, and this search is what keeps a full course query down to a handful of triangles.

constants.name: bounding box sentinel extent
constants.unit: world units, initial extent before the prism pass

constants.name: leaf marker bit
constants.unit: bit mask in a block offset, tested once per tree level

constants.name: leaf offset mask
constants.unit: bit mask in a block offset, applied once per lookup

cards.name: Prism point and sphere test
cards.summary: Each candidate prism is rejected or accepted by three edge plane distances plus a face distance against a skin, then filtered by thickness, type mask and direction of travel
cards.behavior: For a candidate prism the test takes the vector from the prism stored vertex to the query point and projects it onto the three edge normals, subtracting the prism height from the third. A projection at or beyond the skin distance rejects the prism, which leaves only points inside the triangular footprint. The face normal then gives a signed distance measured from the skin, and a prism is skipped when that distance exceeds its thickness plus a small tolerance, so a shallow prism cannot capture a point that is really above it. Directional prism types are skipped when the query movement points along their face normal, which makes triggers one-way. Survivors are filtered by the requested type mask before the routine returns the distance, the face normal and the raw attribute word, and its prism iterator is cleared at the end so the next query starts from the top of the list.

constants.name: narrow phase skin distance
constants.unit: world units, applied once per prism test

constants.name: thickness tolerance
constants.unit: world units, added to the prism thickness test

constants.name: surface distance threshold
constants.unit: world units, tested once per prism

cards.name: Cached collision queries
cards.summary: Repeat queries from almost the same position reuse the last block and prism iterator while a small containment test still holds, avoiding a fresh tree walk for every wheel
cards.behavior: Wheel, body and effect code can ask the course for collision several times per update from almost the same point. Two cached entry points keep the previous query position, its radius and the prism iterator that was current when the walk finished. A new query first tests whether the new sphere lies inside the cached sphere inflated by a skin distance; if it does, the cached iterator is restored and only the movement vector and type mask are updated. If it does not, the block walk runs again and the cache is refreshed. Sphere queries additionally clamp the requested radius to the radius the mesh declares before the walk, so an oversized query cannot force traversal of cells the mesh says cannot contain geometry. The cached path changes only how quickly the prism list is found, never which prisms are considered, so gameplay results are identical between a cold and a warm query.

constants.name: cache containment skin
constants.unit: world units, tested once per cached query

constants.name: cached point query radius
constants.unit: world units, assigned once per cached point query

constants.name: inverse scale numerator
constants.unit: dimensionless numerator, applied once per scaled query

cards.name: Object and drivable collision layers
cards.summary: Course objects carry a small collision mesh in local space, and drivable props answer through a spatial cache before a full walk ever runs
cards.behavior: A course object with collision owns a small packed mesh plus a matrix that places it in the world. A query against the object is transformed into object space, the same prism narrow phase runs there, and the returned offset and bounding box are transformed back, so the kart solver never learns the surface was authored in another frame. When a previous position is not finite, which happens for queries that carry no finite previous position, the object path substitutes an infinite previous position rather than building a movement vector from garbage. Drivable props are registered through the box collision manager under a drivable flag, and a cached query first asks whether the query sphere lies in that spatial cache at all, skipping the whole layer when it does not. The prop path then walks only the registered drivables and unions their individual results, so a course with many movable surfaces costs work proportional to nearby props rather than to every object on the course.

constants.name: local mesh scale
constants.unit: ratio, applied once per object setup

constants.name: drivable cache probe radius
constants.unit: world units, tested once per cached drivable query

cards.name: CPU path offset after a bump
cards.summary: A bumped CPU compares the impact direction with its body forward axis and shifts its path target backwards by an amount scaled between two rate limits
cards.behavior: When a CPU is hit by another kart, the bump direction is dotted with the CPU body forward axis to give an alignment value whose sign says whether the impact came from ahead or behind. The magnitude is mapped into a window between a minimum and a maximum, clamped to the unit range, and used to interpolate between two offset rates, both negative, so the target shifts along the path by an amount that grows with the impact. The resulting offset is applied with the alignment sign and the path handler recomputes the target transform, which is what makes a rear-ended CPU lose its line for a moment instead of continuing as if nothing happened. A purely lateral bump lands on the low end of the rate range while a head-on hit drives the offset furthest. The routine always relays the bump to the look-at handler too, so the driver head turns toward the impact even when the path offset is small.

constants.name: alignment window lower bound
constants.unit: dimensionless alignment, mapped once per bump

constants.name: alignment window upper bound
constants.unit: dimensionless alignment, mapped once per bump

constants.name: smallest path offset rate
constants.unit: path offset units per second at the AI update rate; update rate unverified

constants.name: largest path offset rate
constants.unit: path offset units per second at the AI update rate; update rate unverified

constants.name: alignment clamp
constants.unit: ratio, clamped once per bump

cards.name: Lap checkpoint crossing
cards.summary: A checkpoint sector counts only when two signed side tests agree, using the next checkpoint edge directions and the frame current and previous positions
cards.behavior: Course data stores checkpoints as a left and right edge point with links to the previous and next checkpoint, a lap-check marker and a respawn index. A crossing test takes two positions supplied by the caller and evaluates two signed cross products against the two edge directions stored on the next checkpoint. The first test signs one position against the incoming edge direction, the second signs the other position against the outgoing edge direction, and the sector counts only when both tests agree. Because the test is signed rather than an absolute distance, the two positions must straddle the sector instead of merely being near it, which is what stops a kart parked beside a checkpoint from claiming it. Per-checkpoint player flags record which racers have already claimed the sector, and each checkpoint carries a lap-check marker alongside its link to a respawn point.

constants.name: incoming edge side threshold
constants.unit: signed cross-product units, tested once per sector per update

constants.name: outgoing edge side threshold
constants.unit: signed cross-product units, tested once per sector per update

cards.name: Time trial ghost stream
cards.summary: A recorded ghost is a fixed header plus a separate input area with per-lap times, a drift-mode bit and a checksum over everything except its own trailing word
cards.behavior: A ghost record keeps the driver display name, the date, the Mii data, up to five lap times, the total race time, course, character and vehicle identifiers, the controller type and one bit recording whether automatic drift was used. The input stream does not live inside the header block: the header is a fixed-size prefix and the inputs begin at a fixed offset after it, with their own length field. A record may store those inputs compressed; in that form the stream starts four bytes later so the compression magic can sit in front of it, the size is padded to a word boundary, and the checksum covers the header plus the padded stream. The uncompressed checksum covers the whole buffer except the trailing word that holds the checksum, so a writer can compute the value without a circular dependency. Reading a ghost validates the header before exposing the input stream, and a ghost whose header fails validation reports an empty stream instead of replaying garbage. Capturing the drift mode is what lets a replay interpret the same stick and button words under the same handling scheme.

constants.name: input stream offset
constants.unit: bytes from the record start, fixed per ghost record

constants.name: lap time slots
constants.unit: laps, fixed record layout

constants.name: checksum trailer width
constants.unit: bytes, excluded from the checksum, computed once per write
